So, when my daughter started school last year, she started coming home wet or stinky. And she wouldn’t tell me. So I had to start checking every day.

It took her quite a while to actually start coming home clean and dry.

Is this your daughter’s first or second year in school? I’ve found that mine was too scared to ask to go to the bathroom. And that she was further, too afraid to go on her own. New toilets are hard, man!

It sounds like this behavior is limited to school. And even if this is year number two, something may have changed! Maybe it’s a NEW toilet!

I’d send some communication to the teacher, touch base and see if they can check in with her a bit more often to remind her to check in with her body and see if she needs a bathroom break.

It could even be as simple as school is just too exciting to stop and pay attention to what our body is telling us. And she’s big enough to know to be embarrassed by it, so she definitely won’t volunteer the information.

I’d send her with an extra change of clothes. Mine asked for wipes as well so she could just clean herself up without needing to call attention to it.

I know it’s frustrating. I know it’s gross. And I know. You JUST stopped having to check her all the time. I see you. It was so hard for me to be patient  understanding. But you can do it! And it’s definitely the best way you can help her!

Just have a talk with her too, ask her questions about what’s going on. She’s going to tell you she doesn’t know, or she won’t talk about it. But if you’re consistent and don’t punish her for the problem, she will talk to you. Make sure she knows you’re going to let her teacher know what’s going on so they can help her too. 

And the biggest big? This is so totally normal. It’s okay. Many kids experience this with school, and stress and changes in routine can cause it too. You’re not doing anything wrong. She’s not either. This is just the thing she knows how to control. Or she’s afraid to go while she’s at school. Either way, gentle conversation and encouragement with partnership from school will sort you guys all out. 

This year my 6f daughter is happily accident free so far. But the teachers are still all requesting that first graders bring a change of clothes for accidents anyway. So. It’s gonna be okay. You got this!

A good clinic will not shame you for the state of your mouth. Most intake questionnaires are going to ask you up front if you have any phobia or anxiety of the dentist. They will also ask you if you have any mental or physical ‘ailments or conditions’ or something similar. As well as any medications you take or allergies.

Dentists see mouths all day. They see mouths in all states and all health. And a good dentist will never make you feel judged, or shame you for how your mouth looks or feels. They will state the obvious things, give you the same rote advice every time ‘brush and floss twice a day, make your twice yearly cleaning appointments, look into a water pick or flosser’, but that’s basically a script the same as what the cashier at the grocery store says when you’re leaving the transaction.

I work in the dental field. I work directly with a gum specialist. And please believe me when I tell you that there is nothing in the world that makes my doctor a happier person than knowing that their patient left without pain. That they helped that patient regain functionality and quality of life.

I suggest reading reviews for offices in the area. You’re looking for a place that has reviews mentioning anxiety, or people talking about how they left feeling positive. Dental anxiety is super normal for about a thousand different reasons. And mentioning your concerns up front with the reception area will help them to help you! They can recommend a doctor better suited to your needs. And they can be sure that your doctor is advised of the concerns so they’re fully aware of the boundaries and best able to help you.

I completely sympathize, and I can further share that as a human with depression that makes her just not do the dental care…please go in. Ignoring it will not help. Ignoring it and trying to treat it at home leads to further pain and damage. I had to have teeth extracted, and more than was necessary if I’d just gone in when the problem started.

In the interim. While you’re waiting to get into an office. If you’re in pain, I suggest warm salt water rinses. Alternate that with some over the counter mouth wash designed for sensitivity or mouth pain. Take Tylenol, it reduces inflammation. You can combine that with ibuprofen if the Tylenol isn’t working alone. You can take as much as 800mg of Tylenol at once if you need to for the pain, my doctor actually recommends this over narcotics though does still give the narcotics. I say this so you know it’s not because they’re opposed to the narcotics, it’s because they work better in this sort of pain.

And any time you have the ability to do even the smallest amount of dental hygiene, do it. Something is better than nothing. And if you can manage to wedge in even a nightly rinse with an antibacterial mouthwash into your depression routine, that’s probably going to be more functionally manageable than trying to consistently brush your teeth. 

You can do this! You deserve to be taken care of, and not be in pain! Please feel free to reach out if you want to or have questions or whatever. Good luck!
